chapter: Later career and The Benny Goodman Story
title: The CBS show's producer and the lost tapes
summary: Wilson and Hinton recall producer Bruno Zaratus, the network broadcasts, and the likelihood that tapes sit in CBS's basement.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Yeah, that was a very lucrative era then, and I know that I sure enjoyed it. The trio with you
and Jo Jones, and me being in there with you.
Let's see now; that show, Milt, was produced by a tall young man, Bruno Zaratus.
His father was connected with the New York Philharmonic, like business manager for the New York Philharmonic, because Bruno was producer for that show.
Man, what a memory you have!
No, it just happened to come. The tall young man, Bruno Zaratus.
And Bruno once told me years ago that he had taped all of those shows we did. I often wonder what happened to those taped shows.
They probably have them filed in CBS's basement.
Yeah, they are probably on file at CBS to this day.
I'd be interested to see and hear some of them, because they were some good shows there.
Oh yeah, we had some nice shows.
And that was coast to coast, too.
Yes, that was a network show.
